claims.text: A hierarchical-feature-aware machine-learning model can predict the mechanical properties of HfNbTiVAl10 with lower error than conventional simulations.
Explicitly including interface density, precipitate morphology, and composition gradients will improve prediction accuracy.
HfNbTiVAl10 is polycrystalline and has complex precipitation patterns and gradient grain interfaces.
A gradient-boosting or neural-network model will be trained using hierarchical-interface descriptors, composition, and macroscale test data.
The model is intended for tensile and fracture testing across relevant temperatures and strain rates using standardized specimen geometry.
Hierarchical interfaces and local composition gradients govern dislocation slip, precipitation strengthening, crack initiation, and crack propagation in this alloy.
Local chemical inhomogeneities and morphological features influence dislocation movement and crack-related events.
Capturing local chemistry and morphology will let the model link hierarchical microstructure to mechanical response more accurately than continuum or cluster-based simulations.
The model will reduce Young's-modulus prediction RMSE by approximately 10–20%.
The model will reduce yield-strength prediction RMSE by approximately 10–20%.
The model will reduce fracture-toughness or fracture-strain prediction RMSE by approximately 10–20%.
The model will require 30–40% less computational time for predictions on new compositions or microstructures.
The comparator models do not explicitly incorporate measured hierarchical-interface parameters and approximate local chemistry and structure as more uniform.
Accuracy may deteriorate for phase transformations, metastable interfaces, or processing histories not represented in the training data.
Experimental data for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructures are sparse.
Sparse training data may limit generalization to novel variants and untested conditions.
Independent coupons excluded from training will be tested for Young's modulus, 0.2%-offset yield strength, fracture toughness, and fracture-surface characteristics.
The hypothesis is falsified if combined prediction errors miss the expected improvement range by more than 10%.

contradictions.description: The outcome predicts a 10–20% reduction in RMSE, whereas the falsification rule refers to errors exceeding the improvement range and to 'increasing the RMSE beyond the stated 20% gain.' This mixes error magnitude with percentage improvement and does not define the combined error calculation, making the direction and threshold ambiguous.

The stated conditions concern the as-manufactured HfNbTiVAl10 alloy, while the falsification design calls for new HfNbTiVAl10 compositions and microstructures; the intended compositional scope is therefore inconsistent.
